predecessors.note: The duchy's own dossier dates the elevation to February 1803 (the Recess is dated 25 February); this dossier follows the Recess becoming law on 27 April.

predecessors.note: The abbeys and nine imperial cities of the 1803 Recess (about 850 square miles, 124,000 inhabitants); no dossier of their own.

rulers.title: Prince-elector
rulers.note: Infobox ruler range 1803-1806; the page calls him 'Duke Frederick III' and says he was given the title of King on 1 January 1806.

keyframe_review.note: 9,898 km2. The Württemberg page has no infobox area; it gives only the 1803 increase (about 850 square miles, 2,200 km2, 124,000 inhabitants), so the comparison is unverified: the shape is the right order of magnitude for a duchy plus 2,200 km2. The gazetteer finds the shape at Stuttgart, Reutlingen and Heilbronn; the eastern edge (Ellwangen, Giengen) is thin, which a gap-filler with the Kingdom's area could check.

10,032 km2 (+134 km2 on 1803). The Pressburg gains of Further Austria in Swabia came on 26 December 1805 and are not in this shape; they belong to the Kingdom's 1806 shape. No infobox area to compare.

region.text: the Duchy of Württemberg raised to an Electorate, with the 1803 additions

ledger.note: 1803: the Imperial Recess raises Württemberg to an electorate. 'In 1803, the Imperial diet raised the Duchy of Württemberg to an Electorate' (infobox: 'Raised to Prince-elector: 1803'). The Recess page says 'Baden, Hesse-Kassel, and Württemberg gained status by being made electorates' and that the Recess 'became law on 27 April' (month from that page).

region.text: the abbeys of Ellwangen, Heiligkreuztal, Rottenmünster, Schöntal and Zwiefalten and the imperial cities of Aalen, Esslingen, Giengen, Heilbronn, Reutlingen, Rottweil, Schwäbisch Gmünd, Schwäbisch Hall and Weil (circles of 12 km at ten of them)

ledger.note: 1803: abbeys and nine imperial cities fall to Württemberg. The Recess tables list for Württemberg the ecclesiastical holdings of Ellwangen, Heiligkreuztal, Rottenmünster, Schöntal and Zwiefalten and the imperial cities Aalen, Esslingen am Neckar, Giengen, Heilbronn, Reutlingen, Rottweil, Schwäbisch Gmünd, Schwäbisch Hall and Weil; the Württemberg page: 'nine free imperial cities, among them Reutlingen and Heilbronn and other territories', about 850 square miles. Placed as circles round the towns: the pages give no outline.

region.text: the Electorate, before the Pressburg additions

ledger.note: 1 January 1806: the Elector becomes King. 'On 1 January 1806, Duke Frederick III was given the title of King of Württemberg'; the Pressburg page: Francis II 'recognized the kingly titles assumed by the Electors of Bavaria and Württemberg'. Pressburg also gave 'various parts of Further Austria in the Swabian Circle'; the pages name none, so no gain event is placed here and the Kingdom's dossier carries them. The Electorate closes at 1805 to meet Cliopatria's Kingdom row (1806).

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: French victory; at Pressburg (26 December 1805) Württemberg received parts of Further Austria in the Swabian Circle and its elector was recognised as King.
wars.note: 'Württemberg joined Napoleon on 5 September' 1805. The page does not locate the Austrian lands ceded to Württemberg, so no zone is given.

certainty.note: The pages name abbeys and cities, not boundary lines; the 1803 acquisitions are scattered enclaves and approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's two shapes (9,898 and 10,032 km2) are kept as ok: the pages give no infobox area to test them against, and the gazetteer shows the shape covering Stuttgart, Reutlingen and Heilbronn. The Pressburg gains (various parts of Further Austria in the Swabian Circle) are not placed as a gain here because no page opened names them; the Kingdom of Württemberg dossier should carry them with the counterpart habsburg-monarchy. The 1803 gains are dated to April (the Recess became law on 27 April 1803; the Recess is dated 25 February). The gains name the Holy Roman Empire Minor States row as counterpart, since no dossier exists for the abbeys and imperial cities; the founding event names duchy-of-wurttemberg, whose dossier gives February 1803 for the elevation. The page's article text says the electorate lasted 1803-1805, its infobox 1803-1806; the dossier follows Cliopatria's 1805. Small towns are given as coordinate circles because the gazetteer lacks them.
